# SPEC — Golden fixtures

**NORMATIVE.** These are what let the streams work in parallel: Stream B builds the entire codec and
Stream C builds both apps against real bytes, before `@vadum/core` is finished.

**Owned and generated by Stream 0** (D33, `39-STREAM-0-bootstrap.md`) with a dedicated,
deterministic, offline script — not as a side effect of Phase 0. Committed to `packages/fixtures/`,
**never hand-edited**.

### Three properties, all load-bearing

**1. Fixtures live in their own package, `packages/fixtures`.** They were to live in
`packages/core/src/fixtures/`, which is Stream A's exclusive territory under `20-ARCHITECTURE.md`'s
ownership rule — while Streams B and C must both read them. A read-only package that every stream
depends on and nobody edits removes that contradiction.

**2. The generator needs no chain.** Everything here except a few values is a pure function of fixed
inputs: addresses, derived PDAs, compiled messages, signatures, wire payloads, base45 strings, QR
versions. The exceptions are realistic nonce values and a blockhash, each an opaque 32-byte blob —
**pin them** rather than fetching them.

Phase 0 needs devnet SOL and a funded keypair. Until the first review it was the *only* thing that
could produce fixtures, which made every stream hostage to an owner obtaining devnet funds. Phase 0
still gates spec freeze and Streams A/B/C (G0); it no longer gates writing or running the generator.

**3. The generator is an independent reference implementation** (D33). It depends on `@solana/kit`,
the `@solana-program/*` packages and `qrcode` directly, and **never on any `@vadum/*` package**.
Fixtures produced by the code they are meant to test prove nothing. CI enforces the dependency rule.
The reference modules are exported as `@vadum/fixtures/reference` for tooling only — Phase 0 builds its
payments with them — and CI fails if `packages/core`, `wire`, `client` or `apps/` import them.

### Committed key material — mandatory

The earlier generator called `generateKeyPairSigner()` and **discarded the private keys**. With the
keys thrown away nobody can regenerate a signature, add a case, or extend the set — the fixture file
would have been frozen the moment it was written.

The generator therefore uses **hard-coded seeds and pinned values, written into the script itself**:

```ts
// packages/fixtures/src/seeds.ts
// DEVNET TEST KEYS. Zero value. Deterministic on purpose. Never reuse anywhere real.
export const PAYER_SEED       = new Uint8Array(32).fill(0x01);
export const MERCHANT_SEED    = new Uint8Array(32).fill(0x02);
export const MINT_SEED        = new Uint8Array(32).fill(0x03); // legacy SPL Token test mint (D24)
export const PAYER2_SEED      = new Uint8Array(32).fill(0x04); // D28: the other payer
export const MINT_T22_SEED    = new Uint8Array(32).fill(0x05); // Token-2022 test mint, null hook, zero fee
export const NONCE_VALUE      = '…'; // pinned base58 Nonce — the value a slot is spent against
export const NONCE_VALUE_NEXT = '…'; // pinned — the value after settlement (NONCE_RETURN)
export const NONCE_VALUE_PREV = '…'; // pinned — an earlier value of the same slot (D28 negative)
export const BLOCKHASH        = '…'; // pinned base58 Blockhash — the fresh-path case
```

The file header repeats the warning, and CI greps for it so nobody quietly swaps in real material. The
fixture file's header records both mint addresses and states that each is a **throwaway test mint**,
so nobody reads fixture behaviour as USDC-specific (D24).

> **Do not re-sign and compare.** Safari's Ed25519 implementation is non-deterministic, so the same
> key over the same message produces different valid signatures. The generator runs on Node, whose
> Ed25519 is deterministic, and stores the signature it produced inside `wireAuth`. Consumers
> round-trip and **verify** those bytes; they never sign again and compare the result to a stored
> constant.

---

## Why this file is the contract

`buildMessage` is deterministic — but its determinism is a property of **kit's compiler version**,
not of the Solana protocol (`10-RESEARCH-solana.md` SOL-4). A dependency bump that reorders one
account silently invalidates every signature the system has ever produced, and it would do so quietly.

Golden fixtures turn that into a loud CI failure. This is the single most important regression test
in the project.

---

## File shape

```jsonc
{
  "_warning": "DEVNET TEST KEYS. Zero value. Never reuse.",
  "generator": "packages/fixtures/src/generate.ts",
  "packages": {
    "@solana/kit": "8.0.0", "@solana-program/system": "0.14.0",
    "@solana-program/token": "0.16.0", "@solana-program/token-2022": "0.16.0",
    "qrcode": "1.5.4"
  },
  "mints": {
    "spl": { "address": "<base58>", "description": "Throwaway test mint: legacy SPL Token, 6 decimals … (D24)" },
    "t22": { "address": "<base58>", "description": "Throwaway test mint: Token-2022, null hook, zero fee …" }
  },
  "mintRecords": [ /* one MintRecord per mint, checkedAt: 0 — the DecodeContext.mintCache every case uses */ ],
  "cases": [ /* positive, below */ ],
  "nonceReturn": [ /* below */ ],
  "negative": [ /* below */ ]
}
```

### JSON conventions

Addresses, nonce values and blockhashes are base58 strings. Byte arrays are base64. u64 amounts are
decimal strings, so no consumer loses precision to a JavaScript number. base45 strings are stored
verbatim, spaces included. `@vadum/fixtures` exports the TypeScript types of every shape below
(`src/types.ts`) together with the seeds.

### Positive case

```jsonc
{
  "name": "nonce-dynamic-spl-no-ata",
  "input": {
    "intent": {
      "merchant": "<base58>", "mint": "<base58>", "decimals": 6,
      "amount": "2500000", "lifetime": { "kind": "nonce" },
      "includeCreateAta": false, "tokenProgram": "spl-token",
      "feePayer": "<base58>", "isStatic": false
    },
    "payer": "<base58>",
    "nonceRef": { "index": 0, "value": "<base58>" },
    "amount": "2500000"
  },
  "auth": {                                // what signAsPayer returns and decodeAuth reads — lets
    "payer": "<base58>",                   // core call verifyAuth before wire exists
    "nonceRef": { "index": 0, "value": "<base58>" },
    "amount": null,
    "signature": "<base64>"
  },
  "expectedAmount": null,                  // set in static cases; passed to verifyAuth
  "derived": {
    "nonceAddress": "<base58>",
    "sourceAta": "<base58>",
    "destinationAta": "<base58>"
  },
  "expected": {
    "messageVersion": 0,                   // D18 — never 'legacy'
    "messageBytes": "<base64>",            // exact output of buildMessage
    "messageByteLength": 354,
    "wireFlags": 0,
    "wireIntent": "<base64>",              // exact INTENT (76 B), or STATIC_INTENT (68 B) in static cases
    "wireIntentBase45": "W50…",            // verbatim
    "wireAuth": "<base64>",                // exact AUTH (132 B here), embedding the generator's signature
    "wireAuthBase45": "Y50…",              // verbatim, interior spaces included, NEVER normalised
    "wireAuthBase45Length": 198,
    "qrVersions": { "intent": { "M": 5, "Q": 7 }, "auth": { "M": 8, "Q": 10 } },  // EC-Q is the default (D11)
    "signatureValid": true,                // verified, NOT compared after re-signing
    "fullTransactionLength": 483
  }
}
```

### `NONCE_RETURN` case

```jsonc
{
  "name": "nonce-return-signed",
  "merchant": "<base58>",                  // whose fee-payer key signed
  "statement": {
    "payer": "<base58>", "nonceIndex": 0,
    "spentAgainstValue": "<base58>", "newNonceValue": "<base58>"
  },
  "expected": {
    "signingBytes": "<base64>",            // 118 B: domain tag ‖ payer ‖ index ‖ prior ‖ new (D28)
    "wireNonceReturn": "<base64>",         // 100 B
    "wireNonceReturnBase45": "Z50…",
    "qrVersions": { "M": 6, "Q": 8 },
    "signatureValid": true
  }
}
```

### Negative case

```jsonc
{
  "name": "bad-auth-flags-mismatch",
  "target": "wire.decodeAuth",            // which entry point is under test — see the table
  "input": { "bytes": "<base64>" },       // or { "base45": "…" }, or a structured object for core/client targets
  "context": { "intentFlags": 0 },        // DecodeContext fields, a ledger record, prior queue state, …
  "expectedError": "WIRE_FLAGS_MISMATCH",
  "expectedDetail": {},                   // optional; asserted as a subset of VadumError.detail
  "note": "AUTH flags 0x02 answering an intent with flags 0x00; the length is unaffected"
}
```

`target` is one public entry point, a pipeline written `a → b`, or an array of entry points that must
**each** throw — in which case `input` is keyed by entry point. No stream has to guess what a negative
fixture is testing. Codec contexts name cached mints by address from the header's `mintRecords`;
client contexts carry `limits` (`31-PARAMETERS.md` in base units, with T0's absent cap recorded as u64
max) and the prior `queue` entries.

---

## Required positive cases

| Name | Lifetime | Token program | createATA | Static | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `nonce-dynamic-spl-no-ata` | nonce | spl-token | no | no | The default path (D4) |
| `nonce-dynamic-spl-with-ata` | nonce | spl-token | yes | no | D5 |
| `nonce-static-spl` | nonce | spl-token | no | yes | Static merchant QR (D6); 68 B `STATIC_INTENT`, 140 B `AUTH`, `expectedAmount` set |
| `nonce-dynamic-t22-no-ata` | nonce | token-2022 | no | no | TOK-5; different ATAs, identical instruction data |
| `nonce-dynamic-t22-with-ata` | nonce | token-2022 | yes | no | The Token-2022 ATA branch |
| `fresh-dynamic-spl-no-ata` | fresh | spl-token | no | no | Opt-in fresh path; 108 B `INTENT`, 99 B `AUTH` |
| `nonce-return-signed` | — | — | — | — | The 100-byte payload and its 118-byte signed statement (D20, D28) |
| `base45-double-space` | nonce | spl-token | no | no | An `AUTH` whose base45 form contains two adjacent spaces (about 3% of payloads). The generator starts at `amount = 2_500_000`, increments until one appears, and records the amount. Any whitespace-collapsing step breaks this case (D29) |

Eight positive cases. **Every case must be reproducible from the committed seeds by re-running the
generator**, and CI runs the generator and diffs against the committed file. A generator whose output
drifts from what is committed is the same alarm as a dependency bump changing message bytes.

## Required negative cases — each must throw exactly its code

Written against the check order in `21-SPEC-wire-format.md` (D30): where a payload could break more
than one rule, the table says which bit is set so that exactly one step fails.

### Codec — twenty-one cases

| Name | Target | Expected error |
|---|---|---|
| `bad-version` | `wire.decodeAuth` | `WIRE_VERSION_UNSUPPORTED` — version `0x02` |
| `bad-unknown-type` | `wire.peekPayloadType` | `WIRE_UNKNOWN_TYPE` — type `0x05` |
| `bad-unexpected-type` | `wire.decodeIntent` | `WIRE_UNEXPECTED_TYPE` — given the `nonce-return-signed` payload; `detail` names `INTENT` and `NONCE_RETURN` |
| `bad-reserved-flag` | `wire.decodeAuth` | `WIRE_RESERVED_FLAG_SET` — bit 5 |
| `bad-fee-payer-separate-set` | `wire.decodeIntent` | `WIRE_FEE_PAYER_SEPARATE_UNSUPPORTED` — bit 3 |
| `bad-static-fee-payer-separate` | `wire.decodeStaticIntent` | `WIRE_FEE_PAYER_SEPARATE_UNSUPPORTED` — bits 3 and 4. Step 6 precedes step 7, so not `WIRE_FLAG_NOT_ALLOWED_FOR_TYPE` (D30) |
| `bad-intent-amount-in-auth` | `wire.decodeIntent` | `WIRE_FLAG_NOT_ALLOWED_FOR_TYPE` — bit 4 on a dynamic `INTENT` |
| `bad-nonce-return-flags` | `wire.decodeNonceReturn` | `WIRE_FLAG_NOT_ALLOWED_FOR_TYPE` — bit 0 |
| `bad-static-fresh` | `wire.decodeStaticIntent` | `WIRE_STATIC_CONSTRAINT` — bits 0 and 4 |
| `bad-static-no-amount-flag` | `wire.decodeStaticIntent` | `WIRE_STATIC_CONSTRAINT` — bit 4 clear |
| `bad-length-short` | `wire.decodeAuth` | `WIRE_LENGTH_MISMATCH` — a valid 132 B `AUTH` minus its last byte |
| `bad-length-trailing` | `wire.decodeAuth` | `WIRE_LENGTH_MISMATCH` — plus one byte |
| `bad-auth-flags-mismatch` | `wire.decodeAuth` | `WIRE_FLAGS_MISMATCH` — `AUTH` flags `0x02`, context `intentFlags` `0x00`; length unaffected |
| `bad-mint-unknown` | `wire.decodeIntent` | `MINT_UNKNOWN` — a mint absent from `mintRecords` |
| `bad-decimals-mismatch` | `wire.decodeIntent` | `MINT_DECIMALS_MISMATCH` — decimals 9 for a cached 6 |
| `bad-token-program-mismatch` | `wire.decodeIntent` | `MINT_TOKEN_PROGRAM_MISMATCH` — the `spl` mint with bit 2 set (D30) |
| `bad-base45-out-of-alphabet` | `wire.fromBase45` | `WIRE_BASE45_INVALID` — a lowercase character |
| `bad-base45-bad-length` | `wire.fromBase45` | `WIRE_BASE45_INVALID` — `len % 3 == 1` |
| `bad-base45-group-overflow` | `wire.fromBase45` | `WIRE_BASE45_INVALID` — the group `:::`, which decodes to 91,124 |
| `bad-base45-tail-overflow` | `wire.fromBase45` | `WIRE_BASE45_INVALID` — `000::`: a valid group, then a 2-character tail decoding to 2,024 (D37) |
| `bad-base45-whitespace-collapsed` | `wire.fromBase45` → `wire.decodeAuth` | The `base45-double-space` string with its double space collapsed to one. The generator's own reference decoder records the code: `WIRE_BASE45_INVALID` if a shifted group overflows, otherwise `WIRE_LENGTH_MISMATCH`. Either proves the corruption is loud rather than silent (D29); for the committed payload it is `WIRE_BASE45_INVALID` |

### Core — nine cases

| Name | Target | Expected error |
|---|---|---|
| `bad-signature-tampered` | `core.verifyAuth` | `SIG_INVALID` — one bit of the signature flipped |
| `bad-fee-payer-is-payer` | `core.verifyAuth` and `core.signAsPayer` | `WIRE_FEE_PAYER_IS_PAYER` — an intent whose merchant (and so fee payer) is the payer (D30) |
| `bad-static-amount-mismatch` | `core.verifyAuth` | `CANON_AMOUNT_MISMATCH` — static case with `expectedAmount` ≠ `auth.amount` |
| `bad-static-no-expected-amount` | `core.verifyAuth` | `CANON_AMOUNT_MISMATCH` — static case with `expectedAmount` omitted; `detail.expected` is `null` (D30) |
| `bad-mint-hook-active` | `core.evaluateMint` → `core.assertMintCompatible` | `MINT_INCOMPATIBLE`, `detail.blockers = ['transfer-hook-active']` — input is a `RawMintData` object with `transferHook.programId` set; no chain |
| `bad-nonce-return-wrong-signer` | `core.verifyNonceReturn` | `NONCE_RETURN_UNTRUSTED` — valid signature by a key other than the ledger's merchant |
| `bad-nonce-return-other-payer` | `core.verifyNonceReturn` | `NONCE_RETURN_UNTRUSTED` — the genuine `nonce-return-signed` payload, verified with a ledger for `PAYER2` that has the same slot spent at the same merchant. **The D28 regression test** |
| `bad-nonce-return-other-prior-value` | `core.verifyNonceReturn` | `NONCE_RETURN_UNTRUSTED` — a genuine return whose statement used `NONCE_VALUE_PREV`, verified against a ledger recording `NONCE_VALUE` (D28) |
| `bad-nonce-return-unchanged-value` | `core.verifyNonceReturn` | `NONCE_RETURN_UNTRUSTED` — `newNonceValue` equals the recorded `spentAgainstValue` |

### Client — three cases

Run in `packages/client`'s test suite against an in-memory `KeyValueStore`; `context` supplies prior
queue state.

| Name | Target | Expected error |
|---|---|---|
| `bad-duplicate-auth-live` | `client.queue.accept` | `WIRE_DUPLICATE_AUTH` — the same dedupe key already `queued` |
| `bad-duplicate-auth-settled` | `client.queue.accept` | `WIRE_DUPLICATE_AUTH` — the same dedupe key already `settled` (D31) |
| `bad-t1-without-precheck` | `client.queue.accept` | `LIMIT_PRECHECK_REQUIRED` — tier T1, nonce path, no verdict (D30) |

Thirty-three negative cases. **Negative fixtures matter more than positive ones.** A codec that accepts
everything passes every happy path, and every review of this plan has found real defects that only a
negative suite catches: `base45@2.0.1` silently decoding invalid input, a third of the
`(type, flags)` space having no defined behaviour, and a recovery signature that verified for the
wrong payer.

---

## CI rule

```
for each positive case:                                             # packages/core (A7), packages/wire (B2, B3)
  assert buildMessage(input).messageBytes       === expected.messageBytes
  assert messageBytes[0]                        === 0x80            # v0 marker, D18
  assert encode{Intent|StaticIntent}(intent)    === expected.wireIntent
  assert encodeAuth(auth, flags)                === expected.wireAuth
  assert toBase45(expected.wireAuth)            === expected.wireAuthBase45   # verbatim, no normalisation
  assert fromBase45(expected.wireAuthBase45)    === expected.wireAuth         # round trip
  assert renderQr(…, 'M' | 'Q').version         === expected.qrVersions.*   # one alphanumeric segment (D36)
  assert verifyAuth(intent, auth, expectedAmount) resolves
for nonce-return-signed:                                            # packages/core, packages/wire
  assert nonceReturnSigningBytes(statement)     === expected.signingBytes      # D28
  assert encodeNonceReturn(decodeNonceReturn(x)) === x
  assert verifyNonceReturn(decoded, ledger)     resolves
for each negative case:                                             # the package that owns `target`
  assert target(input, context) throws exactly expectedError, with expectedDetail ⊆ detail
properties (D29):                                                   # packages/wire
  assert no toBase45(randomBytes) ends with ' '                     # 100,000 samples
  assert every positive wire*Base45 starts with W50 | X50 | Y50 | Z50
repository:                                                         # root CI (Stream 0)
  assert regenerating every fixture from the committed seeds reproduces the committed file byte-for-byte
  assert no two @solana/* package versions coexist in the lockfile  # D1
  assert packages/fixtures has no dependency on any @vadum/* package # D33
```

A failure here is never "update the fixture". It is a dependency or a spec change, and it goes to
`02-OPEN-QUESTIONS.md` before anything is regenerated.
